contexts.text: A wall plastered with what is untempered () = what is fictitious appearing as truth.
They plaster it with what is untempered () = that they devise falsities, and make them like truth.

When they build a wall, they plaster it with what is untempered. Say to them that plaster it with what is untempered that the wall shall fall (verses 10, 11) = falsity assumed as a principles, and, by application of the Word as to the sense of the letter, made to appear as truth... What is untempered = what has been falsified. AE 503:9. AE 644:25.
The plastering of what is untempered = the confirmation of what is false.
